Bhoot Bangla (2026) Review
Bhoot Bangla was extremely disappointing and honestly gave me a headache by the end of it. The movie seemed like it was trying very hard to recreate the charm and success of Bhool Bhulaiyaa-style horror comedy, but it failed badly in execution.
The dialogues were weak and poorly written, with very few memorable moments. Instead of being funny or engaging, most scenes felt forced and dull. The film also failed to properly utilize talented actors like Rajpal Yadav, who could have added much more value if given stronger scenes and better comic timing.
The songs were forgettable and unnecessary, adding no real impact to the story. The climax was one of the weakest parts of the film—poorly written, predictable, and completely unsatisfying.
On the technical side, the CGI and VFX were below average and looked cheap in many scenes, which reduced the horror-comedy effect even further. The plot moved very slowly, making the movie feel unnecessarily stretched and boring. Even the cinematography lacked creativity and failed to create the spooky atmosphere the film needed.
Overall, Bhoot Bangla turned out to be a badly executed attempt at horror comedy with poor writing, weak visuals, and wasted performances. Definitely not worth the time.
